'''Dave Goulson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRSE|FRES}} (born 30 July 1965)<ref name=Lady>{{cite news|last=Goulson|first=Dave|title=A Stinging Tale|url=http://www.lady.co.uk/people/features/4267-a-stinging-tale|work=[[The Lady (magazine)|The Lady]]|date=30 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811034018/http://www.lady.co.uk/people/features/4267-a-stinging-tale|archive-date=11 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> is Professor of Biology (Evolution, Behaviour and Environment) at the [[University of Sussex]]. Specializing in the [[ecology]] and conservation of insects, particularly [[bumblebees]], Goulson is the author of several books, including ''Bumblebees: Their Behaviour and Ecology'' (2003), ''Silent Earth: Averting the Insect Apocalypse'' (2021), and more than 200 academic articles. In 2006 he founded the [[Bumblebee Conservation Trust]], a charity that aims to reverse the decline in the bumblebee population.<ref name=Sussex>{{cite web |title=Prof Dave Goulson |url=http://www.sussex.ac.uk/profiles/126217 |publisher=University of Sussex |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190122174247/http://www.sussex.ac.uk/profiles/126217 |archivedate=22 January 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=Guardian>{{cite news|last1=Barkham|first1=Patrick|title=A Sting in the Tale by Dave Goulson – review|url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2013/may/18/sting-tale-dave-goulson-review|accessdate=26 June 2014|work=The Guardian|issue=18 May 2013}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Goulson's upbringing was in rural Shropshire.<ref name=CW>{{cite web|title=Dave Goulson|url=http://www.convilleandwalsh.com/index.php/authors/author/dave-goulson/|website=convilleandwalsh.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160402060140/http://www.convilleandwalsh.com/index.php/authors/author/dave-goulson/|archive-date=2 April 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He attended Adams Grammar School from 1977 to 1982, then [[New College, Telford]] from 1982 to 1984.

He studied biology at [[Brasenose College, Oxford]], then completed a PhD in [[butterfly]] ecology at [[Oxford Brookes University]]<ref name=Sussex/> under the supervision of [[Denis Owen]].

Goulson has said that when he was born in 1965, the [[Bombus subterraneus|British short-haired bumblebee]] was quite widespread, but he never managed to see one before they became extinct in the UK. In his book ''A Sting in the Tale'' (2013), he described a causal link between World War II and the decline of the bee as a result of [[intensive farming]], [[pesticide]] use, and the resultant habitat loss, initially caused by a need to increase wartime food production. "The shorthaired bumblebee died out because its habitats were swept away," he wrote. "It wasn't all that fussy, it just needed enough flowers to feed on: no flowers equals no bees."<ref name=Lady/>

==Career==
Goulson started his academic career at [[Southampton University]] in 1995 as a lecturer in biology, where he began to research the life of bumblebees. In 2006 he transferred to the [[University of Stirling]] as Professor of Biological Sciences.<ref name=CW/> He was awarded the [[Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council]] BBSRC Social Innovator of the Year in 2010.<ref name=BBSRC>{{cite web|title=Innovation and innovators part two – David Goulson |url=http://www.bbsrc.ac.uk/news/policy/2010/101013-f-innovators-innovation-pt2-goulson.aspx |website=BBSRC |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826164806/http://www.bbsrc.ac.uk/news/policy/2010/101013-f-innovators-innovation-pt2-goulson.aspx |archivedate=26 August 2014}}</ref> In 2013 he moved to the University of Sussex as Professor of Biology (Evolution, Behaviour and Environment).<ref name=Sussex/><ref name=Spectator>{{cite news|last1=Mason|first1=Mark|title=A Sting in the Tale, by Dave Goulson – review|url=http://www.spectator.co.uk/books/8913691/saviours-of-the-world/|work=The Spectator|issue=25 May 2013}}</ref> In 2015 he was listed at No. 8 in [[BBC Wildlife]] magazine's list of the top 50 "Conservation Heroes". He serves on the board of trustees of the [[Pesticide Action Network]] and as an Ambassador for [[The Wildlife Trusts]] in the United Kingdom.<ref>[https://profiles.sussex.ac.uk/p126217-dave-goulson Dave Goulson bio], University of Sussex, accessed 25 August 2021.</ref>

==Bumblebee Conservation Trust==
In 2006 Goulson founded the charity the [[Bumblebee Conservation Trust]].<ref name=CW/><ref name=Guardian/> He was well aware that too much scientific research was read only by fellow scientists and that there was a need to engage the wider public: "You can publish experiments in high quality journals again and again but they are only read by a few dozen scientists who work in your field. It achieves little or nothing in the real world."<ref name=BBSRC/>

==Awards==
*(2010). Biotechnology & Biological Sciences Research Council's Social Innovator of the Year Award.
*(2013). Zoological Society of London's [[Marsh Award for Conservation Biology]].
*(2014). British Ecological Society's Public Engagement Award.

*(2013). ''A Sting in the Tale''. London: Jonathan Cape. {{ISBN|0224096893}} (Shortlisted for the [[Samuel Johnson Prize]])<ref name=Guardian/>
